title: Supernova Remnant Puppis A
caption: The supernova remnant Puppis A, imaged by the Dark Energy Camera on the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope
credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA. Image Processing: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab), M. Zamani & D. de Martin (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This image shows Puppis A (Pup A), a supernova remnant, the expanding cloud of debris left behind after a star exploded. It is one of many objects found within a large 1.3-gigapixel image of the Vela Supernova Remnant.

On the sky, Pup A overlaps the Vela Supernova Remnant, but the two are not neighbours. Pup A is four times more distant, roughly 6500–7000 light-years from Earth, and it measures about 100 light-years across.

Supernova remnants glow as their fast-moving gas collides with the thin material between the stars. The filters used here isolate light from oxygen, from sulfur, and from hydrogen-alpha combined with nitrogen, highlighting different parts of the glowing gas. The image was captured with the Dark Energy Camera (DECam), fabricated by the Department of Energy, which works on the NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope in Chile.
scale: Puppis A is about 100 light-years in diameter and roughly 6500–7000 light-years away, according to NOIRLab.

understand.summary: Taken with DECam on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope through [O III], S II and hydrogen-alpha plus nitrogen filters. The colour mapping isn't published.
